standardization: z-score with history mean/std; log for income; budget k=1598 of 4000 (top-k by score, ties by id_candidat)

metric_definitions.eo_gap_vs_merit: TPR(centre) - TPR(remote) among candidates in top-1598 by R; enforced one-sided (remote disadvantage). Overshoot = TPR(remote) - TPR(centre), capped by max_eo_overshoot_vs_merit because hours credit legitimately makes it negative (consensus rule: -0.063).
metric_definitions.eo_gap_vs_consensus: abs(TPR(centre) - TPR(remote)) among positives of the consensus rule
metric_definitions.intersectional_gap: max abs deviation from overall rate over cells remote x first_gen x income tercile (history terciles) with n >= 100
metric_definitions.mean_agreement: mean over the 5 reviewer reference decisions of the share of identical decisions on the 4000 candidates (proxy only)

guard_rules: Overall grant rate in [0.36,0.44] (target 0.38-0.42); budget k=1598 gives 0.3995
Region-blind: no decision keyed on region, distance or postal code; swapping the region label alone changes no decision
Monotone in R: no applicant refused while a lower-R applicant (same programme, same region, same hours band) is granted
Remote vs centre grant-rate gap within each R band (decile/quintile/2-point bins, cells with enough applicants) <= 0.08 (strict 0.05)
Remote vs centre grant-rate gap |DP| <= 0.08 and impact ratio remote/centre >= 0.85
EO gap vs pure-R top-40% reference <= 0.05 in the disadvantage direction; remote overshoot <= 0.09
Intersectional cells (remote x first-gen x income tercile, n >= 100) within 0.10 of the overall rate (>= 0.8-0.85 x overall)
No positive weight on log income (no wealth premium); distance and postal code never in the score
Hours is a small linear credit (<= 0.2 sd), never a penalty and never a threshold cliff
Agreement with the pure-R top-40% decision >= 92%
Per-programme grant rate within 0.10 of the overall rate (reviewers: 0.05 and 0.15)

guard_rules_minority.rule: Per-region grant rate within [0.33,0.45] for each of the 5 regions; remote minus centre in [-0.06,+0.04]
TPR vs pure-R top-39.9% differs by <= 0.05 across the 5 regions
Shuffling region, distance, postal code changes < 1% of decisions
Mean R of granted remote applicants within 0.5 points of granted centre
At fixed R decile, grant rate must not rise with income quintile (spread <= 5 points)
At same R and region, higher hours must not be granted less often
Remote coefficient in a logistic of decision on merit terms within [-0.3,+0.3] logit
No feature with |corr| > 0.5 to region unless justified
Governance: Loi 25 notice of automated decision, human-review path, input/output logging, quarterly subgroup audit

red_flags: Remote grant rate below 0.33-0.34 or impact ratio below 0.83 (historical committee penalty retained; historical remote rate about 0.27)
Remote rate above centre by more than 0.03-0.06 or above 0.44 (over-correction beyond merit)
Distance, postal code or region used directly or via lookalike encoding
Higher-R applicant refused while lower-R applicant granted (same programme/region) without logged reason
Hours or income used as a penalty
Region-specific thresholds, quotas or parity forcing so that remote applicants below the merit cutoff displace higher-R centre applicants

red_flags_minority.flag: Hours used as a threshold or cliff (e.g. above 10 h) rather than a small linear term
Training on decision_octroi without removing the regional penalty
Fairness measured only on a 2-group aggregate, hiding Cote-Nord / Gaspesie gaps
Overall rate at 36% or 44% edge by construction
First-gen or programme used to move decisions
No explanation or human-review path for refused applicants
